reviews.summary: The outer requested-iteration loop invokes the GPU helper once per iteration. Each helper launch uses a ceil-divided grid over dim rows, follows every row's CSR interval, synchronizes and copies the completed vector. All eight emitted architecture variants retain the row-index/dim exit, per-row nonzero arithmetic/backedge(s), and output store.

source_evidence.claim: One CUDA thread maps to each row and reduces rowDelimiters[i]..rowDelimiters[i+1], storing out[i]. The CLI iteration count and nItems set the workload; initialized CSR/operands are passed to spmvGpu in the timed outer loop, whose helper launches a ceil-divided grid, synchronizes, then copies the output.
CUDA architecture list is 60, 61, 62, 70, 72, 75, 80 and 86, all present in the final SASS reviewed.

compiled_evidence.claim: The timed main loop at 1265-1288 calls spmvGpu and increments/branches back at b29b-b2ab. In the helper, CUDA launch/error handling, cudaDeviceSynchronize at bd45 and device-to-host copy follow; this work is inside each count-controlled call.

Across the exact sm_60/61/62/70/72/75/80/86 functions, each row index is compared to dim and out-of-range threads exit. SASS retains DFMA CSR arithmetic and backward loop edges: sm60/61/62 0x0258→0x01b0 and 0x0fb0→0x0580; sm70 0x0258→0x01b0 and 0x0fb0→0x0580; sm72 0x02b0→0x0200 and 0x0e00→0x05e0; sm75 0x02a0→0x01f0 and 0x0df0→0x05d0; sm80 0x0290→0x01e0 and 0x0de0→0x05c0; sm86 0x0280→0x01d0 and 0x0db0→0x0590. Respective STG stores at 0x17d0, 0x17d0, 0x17d0, 0x1500, 0x1500, 0x14f0, 0x14e0 and 0x14a0 store row results.

reviews.summary: The timed host loop launches the grid once for each requested repetition and synchronizes before ending timing. Every row below dim traverses its CSR interval and stores an output. Each of the four configured SASS architecture variants retains row guarding, DFMA nonzero arithmetic, backward traversal branches and stores.

source_evidence.claim: One thread maps to each row, bounds by dim, reduces the CSR interval and stores out[row]. CLI n/s/i and nItems establish dimensions and sparsity; initialized operands are used by the count-controlled timed kernel loop followed by synchronization and output copy.
Configured architectures 60, 70, 80 and 90 correspond to the four inspected SASS variants.

compiled_evidence.claim: Clock starts at 1332, runtime count is checked at 1335-1336, each iteration reaches cudaLaunchKernel at 1401, counter increments/compares/backedges at 1407-1410, and cudaDeviceSynchronize at 1411 precedes stop clock 1414.

For sm_60/70/80/90, row-index-vs-dim tests are followed by exit for invalid threads. DFMA nonzero paths retain backward edges respectively 0x0f98→0x0570, 0x0dc0→0x05a0, 0x0d80→0x0560, and 0x0e10→0x0600; the functions store row results at 0x17b8, 0x14c0, 0x1470 and 0x1550.

source_evidence.claim: Warp row mapping and lane-strided CSR traversal feed a warp reduction and row output. CLI iteration count and matrix setup flow into a timed loop calling spmvGpu once per iteration; the helper launches work for the dimension, synchronizes and copies output.
The selected CUDA target architecture is sm_75, the final SASS variant reviewed.

compiled_evidence.claim: Timed loop starts at 1272, calls spmvGpu at 1286, increments/compares/backedges at 1288-1290. Its compiled helper path launches the kernel, calls cudaDeviceSynchronize at ba15 and copies device output at ba37 before returning.

The source includes a separate output-zeroing/setup path; no separate warmup launch is inferred here.

source_evidence.claim: A thread maps to each row, traverses its entire CSR interval, and stores out[i]. CLI n/s/i sets workload; initialized operands are copied to device, and timed outer loop invokes spmvGpu for every iteration. The helper launches the kernel and copies the result back on each call.
The four selected architectures are sm_60, sm_70, sm_75 and sm_80.

sm_60/70/75/80 all compare row index to dim and exit invalid threads; each retains DFMA and CSR backedges: sm60 0x0258→0x01b0 and 0x0fb0→0x0580, sm70 0x02b0→0x0200 and 0x0e00→0x05e0, sm75 0x0290→0x01e0 and 0x0de0→0x05c0, sm80 0x0280→0x01d0 and 0x0db0→0x0590. reviews.summary: The host passes the CLI iteration count to a timed launch loop. Runtime chooseVectorSize selects one of six kernels (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32 threads per row); each selected SASS function assigns lanes to that row's CSR entries, performs arithmetic and reduces/stores one output per row. All six compiled alternatives retain CSR-controlled backedges and stores.

source_evidence.claim: Kernel maps VECTOR_SIZE threads to a row, has inactive lanes use empty intervals, traverses each assigned CSR index in VECTOR_SIZE strides, reduces and stores once per active row. chooseVectorSize(dispatch includes all six template variants); n/s/i set workload and initialized values/CSR feed the repeated timed launch loop.
Build selects the CUDA target; final SASS contains the six sm_86 template instantiations examined.

compiled_evidence.claim: The measured loop starts at 1440, passes the runtime count into launchSpmv at 1454, and retains its count backedge at 1457-1460; synchronization at 1461 occurs before stop clock at 1464. Compiled launchSpmv contains the vector-size dispatch and calls the selected kernel stub.

Each template function has a row-index/dim predicate and active-lane row handling. The VECTOR_SIZE 32/16/8/4 backedge is 0x04d0→0x02a0; arithmetic DFMA occurs in-loop at 0x0260 and 0x0490-0x04c0; stores are 0x0870/0x0840/0x0810/0x07e0. VECTOR_SIZE 2 retains the same branch 0x04d0→0x02a0 and store 0x07b0; VECTOR_SIZE 1 retains DFMA, backward CSR edge 0x0df0→0x05c0, and store 0x1510. All six selected alternatives therefore retain complete per-row traversal and output.
